newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee ends above lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee ends above lows.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Monday with pared losses as the market recovered from early afternoon lows.
The London market started the week on a firm start but this proved to be shortlived as Indonesian producer hedge selling re-emerged and scale-down roaster buying fizzled out.

September, which stood at $1,765 a tonne at midday pause, carved a new intraday low of $1,755 and dragged down the the New York arabica futures market. The U.S. market had been closed on Friday for a national holiday.
The September contract eventually closed $13 down at $1,785.

"I think the weakeness in London was an effort to get New York to test 165 cents on September. It was successful but it failed to make further inroads as specs and locals were out in New York," said one.
Chartwise, analysts said the market were likely to break out of a chart pennant to test the downside amid a lack of trading volume.
They said the downside break point was $1,780 and then a target of $1,665 at least. An upside break would be a close above $1,855, which would give a target of $2,050.
"But the odds favour a break down," Neil said.
Broker GNI said Brazil's coffee regions would now be frost free through the middle of July based on latest weather forecasts.
"While there is still the possibility of a frost through to the end of August, the risks from here drop sharply," it said.

In other news, the International Coffee Organization (ICO) said producing members' exports reached 81.75 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months to May 1997, up sharply from 73.02 million in the same 1996 period.
In May, exports rose slightly to 7.03 million bags from 7.02 million in April. This compares with 6.60 million in May 1996.
